headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Botpress-to-Pipecat content flow; Pipecat’s shared bus and external API calls raise leakage/conflict concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support chatbot framework and Pipecat ingests text/conversation state over a shared bus, so a plausible path exists for Botpress-generated content to be treated as instructions by Pipecat. No direct provenance or isolation mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Botpress output is forwarded into Pipecat without a provenance or instruction/content separator
IF Pipecat parses shared-bus text as actionable prompts
mitigations: Add a hard delimiter between instructions and content
Strip tool directives from Botpress outputs before handoff
Require a provenance tag on every message
Review one end-to-end sample flow for prompt markers
requires-engineering: add schema validation at the bus boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches text, conversation state, audio, video, and images and can call many third-party APIs; Botpress has no network egress, but if Botpress content is routed into Pipecat, sensitive conversation data can leave the local boundary through allowlisted services. The shared data path is plausible in default Pipecat deployments.
conditions: IF Botpress conversation content is passed into Pipecat services that call external APIs
IF the shared bus carries user text or transcripts containing sensitive data
mitigations: Disable external STT/LLM/TTS providers for sensitive sessions
Redact secrets before forwarding text to Pipecat
Limit the bus to non-sensitive metadata
Check provider allowlists for each Pipecat service
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive workloads in a separate deployment

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Pipecat supports multiple instances with shared-bus state and external service calls. Even without explicit filesystem writes, overlapping mutable runtime state on the bus can cause racey updates or conflicting session handling when both are composed in one workflow.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus or session store
IF Botpress package/runtime changes alter Pipecat integration code during operation
mitigations: Assign separate session namespaces
Serialize writes to shared state
Pin Botpress package versions
Monitor for duplicate session IDs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support responses that Pipecat may ingest as conversation state or downstream text. Because Pipecat integrates many external services, an error or hallucination from Botpress can cascade into speech, transcription, or action routing unless a verification step is inserted.
conditions: IF Pipecat treats Botpress output as authoritative input
IF downstream Pipecat services act on unverified text from Botpress
mitigations: Insert a human or rules-based verification step
Log and sample-check Botpress-to-Pipecat handoffs
Constrain Botpress outputs to structured fields
Disable automatic action-taking on first-pass text
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream execution

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat explicitly handles audio, video, images, text, and analytics and can send data to many third-party providers; Botpress is a support chatbot framework with no egress. If support conversations include regulated data, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches through Pipecat’s external services. Botpress is not cited separately because the compliance risk is driven by Pipecat’s documented data flows.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data is processed through Pipecat providers with different retention or residency terms
IF Botpress conversations include data classes covered by those terms
mitigations: Review provider DPAs before enabling them
Exclude regulated fields from transcripts
Set retention to the minimum available
Document residency for each Pipecat provider
requires-engineering: route regulated traffic to compliant-only services
